summary: All 5 Quick Win items PASS. Backend: 14/14 pytests pass covering canary rollout deterministic bucketing (30% flag → 32.0% observed, 100→100%, 0→0%, matches exact sha1(uid:flag)%100 math), rollout_pct clamping (>100→100, <0→0, str→100 default), task_submitted funnel idempotent stamping pattern + code wiring after task insert, chat_opened funnel first-call writes+stamps + repeat calls idempotent + requires auth, rollback-drill cron boot log present + backend healthy + module importable. Frontend Playwright: stale-tier-cache fix verified (localStorage.aurem_user.tier flipped from 'free' → 'founder' after /auth/me), admin feature flags page shows both flag-rollout-input and per-flag canary badge (flag-rollout-{name} → '🐤 canary: 25% of users').
critical_code_review_comments: services/feature_flags.py:98 — `if pct <= 0 or not user_id: return pct >= 100` — when pct>0 but user_id is None, this returns False. That means any is_enabled() call without a user_id (e.g. anonymous request) for a canary flag falls into the OFF bucket even if 99% rollout. Intentional? Worth a docstring note; call sites that pass user_id=None will silently opt anonymous users out of every partial rollout.

routers/chat.py /opened endpoint accepts an authorization Header without the Optional wrapper — passes None when unauth'd but current_dev() then 401s. Works correctly; minor stylistic — other endpoints use Optional[str] = Header(None, alias='Authorization').

The is_enabled service module reads the whole feature_flags collection into an in-memory cache every 60s but has no upper bound; if the collection ever grows to thousands of flags this is fine, but worth capping/paginating eventually.

Admin /feature-flags POST is idempotent upsert but has no soft-delete; the test flag 'test_canary_quickwin' had to be cleaned via direct Mongo. Consider a DELETE endpoint for future cleanup ergonomics.
